name: ProofForge
headline: ProofForge turns Meta's Muse models into provers of financial code.
summary: Each task states what financial code must guarantee as locked Lean 4 requirements. ProofForge refutes code that breaks one with a counterexample the Lean kernel checks, and accepts a fix, written by Muse Spark or by people, only when six independent kernels check its proof. Every verdict is a Passport, bound by hash to the specification, the source and the executable, that anyone can re-run.

checking.judge: lake comparator --paranoid in a fresh bubblewrap sandbox with six kernels (Lean default and paranoid, lean4lean, nanoda, con-leche, con-ron), then leanchecker and an axiom audit; the executable rebuilt from the same source runs generated property cases

loss_total.note: the sum of the loss figures quoted for the incidents, each rounded down; the figures measure different things (taken, net profit to the attacker, realized loss), as each states

flagships.system: concentrated-liquidity pools of Cetus, a DEX on Sui

loss.basis: taken, as The Block reports from Cetus's incident report

flagships.bug: The overflow check in checked_shlw tested against a 256-bit limit instead of a 192-bit limit, so a shift that lost bits reported no overflow.

property_proved.text: The overflow check never loses a bit, so a deposit is always charged at least the exact amount it owes.

vulnerable_code.label: Original checked_shlw
vulnerable_code.finding: On the attack deposit it charges 1 unit of token A; the exact amount owed, rounded up, is 31572840708638430117170542 units.

versions.detail: integer-mate at 4d09c8b, the last commit before the fixes
versions.finding: The attack deposit is charged 1 unit of token A. The exact amount owed, rounded up, is 31572840708638430117170542 units, about 3.16 × 10^25.

It refuses the attack deposit, but checkedShlw(2^192) = (0, false): 2^192 shifted left by 64 bits wraps to 0 and no overflow is reported. A deposit with liquidity × price difference = 2^192 is charged 0.
All five requirements proved for every 256-bit input and every u128 price and liquidity.

versions.detail: from the original code, accepted on the first attempt
versions.finding: All five requirements proved. A separate theorem, muse_eq_pr7, proves it returns the same value and overflow flag as the final fix on every 256-bit input.

muse_repair_equivalent_to_upstream_fix.theorem: theorem muse_eq_pr7 : ∀ n : BitVec 256, museShlw n = pr7Shlw n

real_code.summary: real Move code at 3 pinned commits, 2,007 inputs
real_code.result: 658 break a requirement on the original, 0 on the final fix
real_code.method: The real checked_shlw and get_delta_a, unmodified at each pinned commit, ran with Sui CLI 1.83.0 (sui move test) on 2,007 inputs: 7 documented values and 2,000 generated by the task oracle.

results.note: identical to the Muse repair on every input

not_proved: The Move code is run on 2,007 inputs and compared with the Lean ports and the proved component; it is not itself proved.
get_delta_b, the tick math and the rest of the pool (positions, swaps, fees) are not specified.

flagships.system: Composable Stable Pools of Balancer V2 and its forks

loss.basis: across Balancer and its forks, as OpenZeppelin reports; The Block reports estimates of over $128 million

flagships.bug: A swap for an exact amount out rounded that amount down before pricing it, so 17 wei of osETH, worth 17.988 of the pool's units, was priced as 17.
flagships.context: Certora writes that its 2022 verified properties of these pools “did not constrain the relationship between individual swaps or rounding behavior”. The locked requirements here are about exactly that.

property_proved.text: For any pool math meeting the stated contract, no batch of swaps of any length lowers the pool's value.

vulnerable_code.label: Deployed swap path of the osETH/WETH pool
vulnerable_code.finding: Four rounds of the attack's three swaps lower the pool's value from 4,749,898,000 to 297,229,191.

muse_repair.change: rounds the amount out up before pricing it and refuses the swap unless that amount is below the pool's balance

attack.text: The attacker sells BPT for the pool's tokens, 22 swaps in one batch. BPT swaps, joins and exits are not modeled.
attack.after: 67,000 wei of WETH and 67,000 of osETH

attack.text: It takes osETH out until 18 wei are left.
It takes 17 wei of osETH out. At the cached osETH rate that is 17.988 of the pool's units; the pool rounds it down and prices 17.
It takes WETH out, paid with osETH, and repeats the three swaps, 30 rounds in all.
attack.after: 889 wei of WETH and 1,472 of osETH

attack.text: It buys BPT back at the collapsed price. This step is not modeled; the specification states the property it relied on.

flagships.kernel_checked_outcome: The kernel checks that four rounds of these swaps lower the pool's value from 4,749,898,000 to 297,229,191, and that the port, run with a port of StableMath, charges exactly the logged amount of all 90 swaps of the attack.

real_code.summary: deployed Vault and pool on an Ethereum fork, 501 batches
real_code.result: identical to the Lean port on all 501; the pool's value falls in 56, never with the Muse repair
real_code.method: On a fork of Ethereum taken just before the attack transaction, the attack's first 22 swaps brought the deployed pool to 67,000 wei of each token, as on chain. Then 501 batches (the attack's 90 swaps and 500 generated, 10,385 swaps in all) ran through the deployed Vault, the Lean port and the Muse repair.

results.note: the pool's invariant falls in 56 batches, and its BPT price with it
the proved component on the same 501 batches

not_proved: The requirements hold for any pool math meeting a stated contract; a constant-product pool is proved to meet it, StableMath is not, so results with StableMath are tested.
BPT swaps, joins and exits are not modeled. The deployed contracts are run on 501 batches on a fork; they are not themselves proved.

loss.basis: in net profit to the attacker, as Cyfrin reports; CoinDesk later reported that all recoverable funds were returned

flagships.bug: donateToReserves moved an account's collateral to the reserves without the liquidity check that withdraw, mint and transfer perform.

property_proved.text: No sequence of operations leaves any account with more debt than its risk-adjusted collateral.

vulnerable_code.label: Euler v1 at b1ee326
vulnerable_code.finding: The attack sequence leaves 134,000,000 of debt with no collateral behind it.

muse_repair.change: adds the health check to the donation guard

attack.text: The violator deposits 20,000,000, then mints 200,000,000, repays 10,000,000 and mints 200,000,000.
The violator donates 100,000,000 eTokens to the reserves. No liquidity check runs.
A second attacker account liquidates 256,000,000 of the debt at the 20% maximum discount.
The liquidator withdraws the whole pool, 38,904,507: the lender's entire deposit.

flagships.kernel_checked_outcome: The kernel checks every state above and that NoBadDebt, StaysHealthy and ActorHealthy are false for the port: 134,000,000 of debt is left with no collateral behind it.

real_code.summary: real Solidity contracts at the pinned commit, 1,004 sequences
real_code.result: 57 break a requirement unmodified, 0 with the missing check added
real_code.method: The unmodified contracts at b1ee326 were deployed in a local Foundry test and run on the attack, Euler's three donate test scenarios and 1,000 generated sequences, then compared after every operation with the requirements, with Euler's own liquidity computation and with the Muse repair.

results.note: Euler's own liquidity check also reports collateral below liability in 57
a local copy, not an upstream release

not_proved: One asset priced at 1, an eToken exchange rate fixed at 1 and no interest; flash loans, sub-accounts and multiple collateral assets are not modeled.
The contracts are run on 1,004 sequences and compared with the requirements and the proved component; they are not themselves proved.

flagships.system: SMARS, Knight Capital's equity order router
flagships.reconstructed: Knight Capital is reconstructed from the SEC's findings (Release No. 34-70694) because Knight's code is not public; nothing in the task is Knight's code, and every Knight Passport says so.

loss.basis: realized loss, as the SEC order states

flagships.bug: New code was not copied to one of eight servers. There, orders carrying a repurposed flag ran dead Power Peg code, which kept sending child orders without counting the executions.
flagships.context: The SEC order reports millions of child orders for 212 parent orders: 4 million executions in 154 stocks, more than 397 million shares, in about 45 minutes.

property_proved.text: On every server and code version, after any sequence of events, the shares sent for an order never exceed its quantity.

vulnerable_code.label: Reconstructed Power Peg router
vulnerable_code.finding: For every n, n rounds of a 100-share routing opportunity and a fill send n child orders and 100 × n shares for one 100-share order.

muse_repair.change: removes the Power Peg path, so every build routes by the shares not yet sent and every fill advances the executed count

attack.text: Seven of eight servers run the new code; the eighth still runs the old code (paragraph 15).
A parent order for 100 shares arrives with the repurposed flag, which on the eighth server activates Power Peg (paragraphs 13 and 16).
A routing opportunity for 100 shares arrives. The router sends a 100-share child order, and it is filled.
Power Peg's count never sees the fill, so the next opportunity sends another 100 shares, and so on for every opportunity.
attack.after: after n rounds: n child orders, 100 × n shares executed

flagships.kernel_checked_outcome: The kernel proves by induction that the reconstructed router sends n child orders for one 100-share order, for every n, while the new code sends exactly one on the same events. It also refutes the obvious patch: counting fills again still sends 200 shares for a 100-share order when two opportunities arrive before a fill.
flagships.real_code: none: the code is not public
not_proved: The mechanism by which fills stopped reaching Power Peg's count is one interpretation of paragraphs 14 and 16 of the order; other mechanisms with the same outcome are possible.
Prices, venues, order types, timing and cancellations are not modeled. The executable wrapper is tested, not proved.

flagships.system: hWBTC market of Hundred Finance, a Compound v2 fork on Optimism

loss.basis: in reported losses (rekt.news gives $7.4M; this figure was not checked here)

flagships.bug: redeemUnderlying rounded the shares burned down, so a withdrawal worth 1.99999999992 share units burned 1.

property_proved.text: No sequence of operations, donations included, lowers the value of a share while shares are outstanding.

vulnerable_code.label: Hundred hToken share accounting
vulnerable_code.finding: After the attack's own amounts, the last share unit is backed by 2 satoshi.

muse_repair.change: prices shares from the exact ratio of assets to supply and rounds the shares burned up

attack.text: The market is emptied: no shares outstanding, 1 satoshi of cash.
It sends 50,030,063,816 satoshi straight to the market, so each unit is worth about 250 WBTC, and borrows ETH against its 2 units. Borrowing is not modeled.
It withdraws 50,030,063,815 satoshi, worth 1.99999999992 share units. The contract burns 1.

flagships.kernel_checked_outcome: The kernel checks that the port breaks REQ-SHARE-VALUE (a share falls from 50,030,063,817 / 2 satoshi to 2) and REQ-WITHDRAW-ROUNDS-UP. The Muse repair burns both share units.

real_code.summary: deployed bytecode on an Optimism fork, 501 sequences
real_code.result: matches the Lean port on all 501; 292 break a requirement
real_code.method: On a fork of Optimism at block 90761917, the hWBTC market was emptied as in the attack, and 501 sequences (the attack and 500 generated) ran on the deployed CErc20Delegate bytecode, on the Lean port and on the Muse repair.

results.note: identical to the Lean port after every operation of all 501
the proved component, on the same 501 sequences

not_proved: Only share accounting is modeled; the comptroller, borrowing, liquidation, interest and reserves are not. The specification states the share-value property the borrow relied on.
The deployed contract is run on 501 sequences on a fork and compared with the port and the requirements; it is not itself proved.

muse_alone_vs_proofforge.note: Every run is Muse Spark 1.3 (Contributor tier), capped at $10 at list prices and 14400 s, and judged by ProofForge against the same locked specification. A0: Muse alone, compile-and-retry with Lean's errors and the axiom audit. A1: the ProofForge harness. A2: A1 with Muse Wonder 1.0 as lemma planner. On these tasks the harness did not complete more tasks than Muse alone; the refutations, the specification and the check are ProofForge's.

open_weight_models.serving: self-hosted with vLLM on one Modal H100

scope: ProofForge proves the logic of code against a written specification. It does not protect keys, servers, oracles, bridges or other infrastructure, and it does not prove the deployed Solidity or Move bytecode itself.
not_claimed: The deployed Solidity and Move code is not itself proved. Each incident's Lean 4 port is a reviewed hand translation, tested against the real code on the stated inputs; the translation is not machine-checked.
A requirement covers exactly what its Lean statement says. Each port models only the logic named in its task README.
Loss figures are quoted from the sources each task README cites.
The JSON wrapper around each proved function is tested, not proved.
Knight Capital is reconstructed from the SEC's findings (Release No. 34-70694) because Knight's code is not public; nothing in the task is Knight's code, and every Knight Passport says so.
